To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytoplasmatic domain of FlhB is required for the export of flagellin; and that the cytoplasm of Salmonella cells expressing the AquSalFlgB chimera is depleted of ubiquinone.
the cytoplasmically localized C-terminal domain of FlhB, which is highly conserved among FlhB orthologs, is essential for the assembly of the type III flagellar export apparatus.

a cross-complementation of the type III flagellar export apparatus with the AquSal FlhB chimera results in the loss of flagella and the loss of motility and this is due to the reduction of the quinone biosynthesis in the cytoplasmatic membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the type III flagellar export apparatus.
the study of the mechanism of type III secretion and the role of the quinone respiratory pool in flagella biogenesis.
the study of a bacterial type III export system, the flagellum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FlhB membrane protein of the bacterial flagellate is essential for flagellum biogenesis.
the FlhB protein is essential for flagellar assembly and motility and the FlhB cytoplasmic region is important for the function of the export apparatus.
the cytoplasmatic domain of FlhB is important for flagellar biogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cytoplasmatic domain of Salmonella and Aquifex FlhB is interchangeable but their trans-membrane domains have different requirements for the assembly of the export apparatus and the export of the flagellar components.
the quinone biosynthesis pathway is important for flagellar assembly.
the quinone level of the cytoplamic membrane is a limiting factor for the export apparatus of the flagellin and that FlhB is the protein that senses the level of quinone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type III export system of the flagellin and the needle complex is very similar and the cross-complementation of the FlhB protein from A. aeolicvs to S. typhimurium is possible.
a single amino acid change in a trans-membrane helix of FlhB can cause a dramatic reduction in motility.
the type III export system in Salmonella is very sensitive to the presence of an ortholog of FlhB from a distant bacteria.
